summary: Iteration 3 backend testing complete for Omega Chat. All 65 pytest tests pass (36 regression from iter 1+2, plus 29 new iter-3 tests). New coverage: (1) GET /api/auth/me now returns display_name and username — both null for fresh-signup stub users; (2) GET /api/auth/username-available — 401 without auth, {available:true, username:<normalized_lc>} for valid unused, {available:false} for taken, {available:false, reason} for too-short/too-long/symbol/reserved (admin, omega). Uppercase input is normalized+accepted. Checking one's own currently-claimed username returns available=true; (3) POST /api/auth/complete-profile — 401 without auth, trims display_name, validates length 1–40, rejects usernames not matching ^[a-z0-9_]{3,20}$, normalizes uppercase to lowercase, rejects reserved names (400), returns 409 on conflict (case-insensitive: @ALICE also 409), allows same user to re-submit (change display_name and/or change username); (4) Search by @username with GET /api/users/search?q=@alice — matches username prefix case-insensitively, excludes self; (5) Search without @ prefix now also matches display_name and username fields (regression-friendly for name/email too); (6) Sparse/partial unique index verified — two users can both have username=null (no dup-key), and one can claim a username without affecting the other. Direct DB insert of 2 null-username stub users succeeds. MongoDB _id is not leaked in any response.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py validate_username lowercases input before regex-check, so mixed-case usernames like 'Alice' are accepted and normalized — matches spec. Good.

server.py /auth/username-available catches HTTPException from validate_username to return 400-detail as 'reason' in a 200 body — this is a good UX pattern (client doesn't need to distinguish 200 vs 400). Verified working.

Partial unique index on username with partialFilterExpression={username: {$type: 'string'}} correctly allows multiple docs with missing/null username. Confirmed by direct DB inserts and by fixture-based fresh users all coexisting.
search_users returns up to 50 rows unbounded on empty q — could be expensive at scale; consider requiring q.strip() length >= 1 in prod. Non-blocking.
server.py still uses deprecated @app.on_event startup/shutdown handlers (carried over from iter 1). Non-blocking.

ProfileUpdate model requires both display_name and username to be sent on every POST /complete-profile — even for renaming just one field. This is fine per current spec (client always sends both), but worth documenting.
